To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a class of flows with the polyhedral reachability property, and that we have identified classes of flows with the strongly polyhedral and polyhedrallly sliced properties, and we have discussed an application to approximate exponential behaviours.

(1) the polyhedral flow property is preserved when the rates of the flow are allowed to depend on the current state; (2) it is not preserved when the rates depend on the previous state; (3) it is preserved if the rates depend on a fixed time interval in the past; (4) it is not in general preserved if the rates are allowed to depend arbitrarily on the previous states, but it can be preserved in some special cases.

(i) the subclass of flows described by linear origin-dependent rate polyhedra is a superset of the subclass of flows that are strongly polyhedral; (ii) the subclass of strongly polyhedral origin-dependent rate polyhedral flows is a superset (but not a subset) of the subclass of polyhedrally-sliced flows, and (iii) both subclasses are superset (but neither is a subset) of polyhedral flows.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether we can generalize the semantics of linear hybrid automaton for describing flows without compromising the polyhedral nature of the flows, and the consequent simplifications in verification procedures.
a generalization of the syntax of linear systems for hybrid automata that is compatible with the existing symbolic fixpoint computation techniques.
the study of the class of flows in hybrid automata that preserve the polyhedral structure of the set of reachable states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a class of hybrid automata, we can replace the linear flows by polyhedral ones while preserving the property of polyhedrality of the set of states reachable from a given polyhedral initial set.
the class of flows that we study is a proper subclass of linear hybrid systems, but it is a proper superset of linear hybrid systems.
the class of flows that we can handle is the one of strongly polyhedrally-sliced flows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we study flows in which the rates can be described by origin-dependent polytopes, and that the resulting flows can be polyhedrally described.

we study the class of flows for which the set of reachable states starting from a polytope can be described by a polytope, and show that it is a proper superset of the class of flows described in the literature.

we provide a formal characterization of flows that are compatible with polyhedral analysis, and we provide a formal definition of a class of flows that can be used as an approximation for exponential behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the polyhedral class of flows is a very restrictive subclass of linear hybrid flows, it is possible to generalize it in a controlled way to obtain classes of flows that are more expressive than linear hybrid flows, while still retaining the polyhedral properties.
, for the subclass that we study, it is possible to generalize the syntax of hybrid automata for expressing flows without sacrificing the key property of polyhedral flows.
, for a large class of flows, the set of reachable states from a polyhedric set of initial states remains polyhedric.
